svg.desc: Selected documented stages, arranged in reading order. Equal spacing and box size do not encode elapsed time, contamination level, risk, cost, causal weight or policy effectiveness. The diagram is an EPA-sourced chronology, not a complete community history or independent health assessment. AI source review is not human editorial approval.
svg.text: Times Beach: contamination, flood, relocation and cleanup
Selected stages documented in the U.S. EPA Region 7 retrospective

g.aria-label: Early 1970s: Contaminated mixture used for dust suppression
g.text: EPA says a dioxin and waste-oil mixture was sprayed at more
than 25 Missouri locations, including Times Beach.

g.aria-label: November 1982: Town receives first contamination warning
g.text: EPA identifies this as Times Beach's first news of possible
dioxin contamination and records soil sampling.

g.aria-label: December 1982: Flood, evacuation and no-return recommendation
g.text: Record Meramec River flooding forced evacuation; CDC and EPA
recommended that the town not be reinhabited.

g.aria-label: 22 February 1983: Federal and state buyout announced
g.text: EPA announced a Superfund-funded buyout covering 800
residential properties and 30 businesses after recommending
permanent relocation for more than 2,000 residents.
The decree allocated excavation, transport, demolition,
incinerator construction, operation and long-term management
EPA records the temporary incinerator in 1996 and marks
cleanup completed in 1997; materials came from Times Beach and

g.aria-label: 1999–2001: State park opens; site later leaves NPL
g.text: State park opens; site later leaves
Route 66 State Park opened on the former town site in 1999.
EPA deleted Times Beach from the National Priorities List in
EPA Region 7 reports that sampling confirmed no significant
health risk for workers or visitors at Route 66 State Park.
